title: Periappendiceal abscess after perforated appendicitis: Bacteroides fragilis (anaerobe)
vignette: A 22-year-old man comes to the emergency department due to fever, abdominal pain, and vomiting. He has had these symptoms for the past 4 days but has not sought medical attention because of concerns over the cost of treatment. On examination, the patient appears acutely ill. There is right lower quadrant tenderness with rebound as well as a palpable mass. CT scan of the abdomen and pelvis demonstrates a periappendiceal fluid collection. Culture of this fluid would most likely isolate which of the following organisms?

clues.text: right lower quadrant tenderness with rebound as well as a palpable mass
clues.note: RLQ peritonitis with a palpable mass after several days suggests perforated appendicitis that has walled off into an abscess.
A periappendiceal fluid collection = intraabdominal abscess from perforated appendicitis; such infections are polymicrobial and often yield anaerobes like Bacteroides fragilis.

whatMatters: A periappendiceal ABSCESS from perforated appendicitis is POLYMICROBIAL colonic flora. Of the choices, BACTEROIDES FRAGILIS - an anaerobic gram-negative bacillus whose capsular polysaccharide FAVORS ABSCESS formation - is the most likely isolate. Answer D.
strategy: Recognize the intraabdominal (colonic-source) abscess and pick the anaerobe most associated with abscesses: Bacteroides fragilis (and E coli among aerobes). Reject organisms not typical of a periappendiceal abscess: S aureus (skin abscesses), Actinomyces (cervicofacial/less common), Candida albicans (usually after proximal-bowel perforation/immunosuppression), and Entamoeba histolytica (amebic LIVER abscess, unrelated to appendicitis).

eliminations.label: Staphylococcus aureus - skin abscesses
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: a gram-positive coccus that causes skin/soft-tissue abscesses. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: it is not a typical isolate from an intraabdominal (colonic) abscess. ✅ Correct if: cutaneous abscess/furuncle.

eliminations.label: Actinomyces - less common, cervicofacial
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: an anaerobic filamentous bacterium forming abscesses (cervicofacial 'lumpy jaw,' sometimes abdominal with sulfur granules). ❌ WHY IT FAILS: it is much less common than B fragilis and less likely in an acute periappendiceal abscess. ✅ Correct if: chronic abscess with sulfur granules/sinus tracts.

eliminations.label: Candida albicans - proximal-bowel perforation/immunosuppression
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: a yeast that can complicate proximal-bowel (e.g., perforated peptic ulcer) infections or immunosuppression. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: it is not the usual isolate from an appendiceal abscess. ✅ Correct if: perforated proximal bowel or immunocompromise.

eliminations.label: Entamoeba histolytica - amebic liver abscess
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: a protozoan causing dysentery and 'anchovy-paste' amebic LIVER abscess. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: it is unrelated to perforated appendicitis/periappendiceal abscess. ✅ Correct if: liver abscess after dysentery/travel.

reasoning: Perforated appendicitis walls off into a periappendiceal abscess
Bacteroides fragilis is a common anaerobic isolate whose capsule promotes abscess formation
mechanism: Perforated APPENDICITIS spills COLONIC FLORA into the peritoneal cavity, which can wall off into a PERIAPPENDICEAL ABSCESS. Intraabdominal infections are POLYMICROBIAL, and the most prominent isolates are BACTEROIDES FRAGILIS (an anaerobic, non-spore-forming gram-negative bacillus) and ESCHERICHIA COLI (a facultative gram-negative rod), along with other enterococci and streptococci. B fragilis is especially associated with ABSCESS formation because its surface CAPSULAR POLYSACCHARIDE promotes abscess development and helps it evade host defenses; it also produces enzymes and grows in the low-oxygen abscess environment. Management combines source control (drainage/appendectomy) with antibiotics that cover anaerobes and gram-negative enterics (e.g., metronidazole plus a broad-spectrum agent, or a beta-lactam/beta-lactamase inhibitor). The distractors are not typical periappendiceal-abscess isolates: S aureus (skin), Actinomyces (cervicofacial/uncommon), Candida (proximal-bowel/immunosuppressed), and Entamoeba histolytica (amebic liver abscess).

difficulty.label: 🧠 Knowledge
difficulty.text: First Aid Micro > intraabdominal abscess: polymicrobial colonic flora; Bacteroides fragilis (anaerobic gram-negative bacillus; abscess-promoting capsule) + E coli are most prominent; treat with source control + anti-anaerobe/gram-negative antibiotics (metronidazole).

difficulty.label: 📖 Comprehension
difficulty.text: Perforated appendicitis -> periappendiceal abscess -> Bacteroides fragilis (anaerobe).

difficulty.label: 🔤 Vocab
difficulty.text: Unsure on Bacteroides fragilis, anaerobe, polymicrobial intraabdominal infection, or capsular polysaccharide? Tell me which.

difficulty.label: 🨤 Distractor
difficulty.text: S aureus = skin abscess; Actinomyces = cervicofacial/uncommon; Candida = proximal-bowel/immunosuppressed; Entamoeba = liver abscess.

difficulty.label: 🗒️ Other
difficulty.text: Bank: intraabdominal (appendiceal) abscess = polymicrobial; Bacteroides fragilis + E coli most prominent.

firstAid.detail: Micro > S aureus (skin), Entamoeba (liver), Candida, Actinomyces.

memoryHook: A walled-off belly abscess from a burst appendix is a colonic-bug party - the anaerobic ringleader that loves making abscesses is Bacteroides fragilis.
